catalogTopics.method: Question-content review against current CED; scanned page checked

candidates.name: Lewis structures
candidates.definition: Drawing or interpreting Lewis electron-dot diagrams: counting total valence electrons, placing bonding and lone pairs, multiple bonds, octet exceptions and polyatomic-ion charges.
candidates.include: Tag when the student must draw a Lewis structure, or must determine bonding and lone pairs that are not shown in order to answer.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag when a complete Lewis structure is given and is only read for a later step that is tagged separately, unless reading it requires electron counting.

candidates.name: Galvanic and electrolytic cells
candidates.definition: Identifying the anode (oxidation) and cathode (reduction), electron flow, salt-bridge ion migration and electrode changes in galvanic and electrolytic cells.
candidates.include: Tag when cell components, half-reactions at each electrode, electron or ion flow, or electrode mass changes must be identified.
candidates.exclude: Assigning + and - labels to electrodes is not assessed; do not tag voltage calculations alone (tag cell-potential).

candidates.name: Gibbs free energy and favorability
candidates.definition: Using ΔG° = ΔH° - TΔS° and the signs of ΔH and ΔS to determine thermodynamic favorability and the temperature at which favorability changes.
candidates.include: Tag when ΔG must be calculated or its sign reasoned from ΔH and ΔS, or a crossover temperature found.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag ΔG-K or ΔG-E relationships alone (tag free-energy-equilibrium or cell-potential).

candidates.name: Electron-domain counting
candidates.definition: Counting the electron domains around a central atom, where each lone pair and each bond (single, double or triple) counts as one domain.
candidates.include: Tag when the answer depends on counting domains, including the rule that a multiple bond is one domain, as a supporting step for geometry or hybridization.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag when geometry or hybridization is simply recalled for a familiar molecule without domain reasoning being needed.

candidates.name: Formal charge
candidates.definition: Calculating the formal charge on atoms in a Lewis structure and using formal charges to judge which of several structures best represents a species.
candidates.include: Tag when formal charges must be calculated, compared, or used to choose the preferred structure, even if the words 'formal charge' do not appear.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag oxidation numbers (tag oxidation-numbers) or a Lewis structure question whose answer does not depend on formal charge.

candidates.name: Molecular geometry (VSEPR)
candidates.definition: Predicting electron-domain geometry and molecular shape from the arrangement of bonding and lone-pair domains around a central atom.
candidates.include: Tag when a molecular or electron-domain geometry must be named, identified, drawn or used.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag hybridization-only questions (tag hybridization) or bond-angle questions where shape is given (tag bond-angles).

candidates.name: Orbital hybridization
candidates.definition: Assigning sp, sp2 or sp3 hybridization to an atom from its number of electron domains.
candidates.include: Tag when the hybridization of an atom must be stated or used.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag geometry-only answers; d-orbital hybridization, drawing hybrid orbitals and molecular-orbital diagrams are not assessed.

candidates.name: Organic nomenclature and functional groups
candidates.definition: Naming organic compounds, identifying functional groups and isomers as a goal in itself. Not assessed on the current AP Chemistry exam.
candidates.include: Tag legacy questions whose main demand is organic naming, isomer counting or functional-group identification.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag questions that merely use organic molecules as context for Lewis structures or intermolecular forces.

candidates.name: Ion charges and ionic formulas
candidates.definition: Predicting common ion charges from valence electrons and periodic position, and writing charge-neutral ionic formulas.
candidates.include: Tag when the student predicts an ion's charge, the formula of an ionic compound, or explains ion formation from electron configuration.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag routine use of a given ionic formula in a calculation.

candidates.name: Resonance and delocalization
candidates.definition: Representing a species with two or more valid Lewis structures, understanding the real structure as a hybrid with delocalized electrons, and the resulting equal or fractional bond orders.
candidates.include: Tag when resonance structures must be drawn or identified, or when delocalization explains equal bond lengths or stability.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag isomers (different atom connections) or a single Lewis structure with no alternative arrangement.
